title: Empirical, theoretical, and practical advantages of the HEXACO model of personality structure
claimSupported: Cross-cultural structural validity of the 6-factor HEXACO model and distinctiveness of Honesty-Humility from Big Five Agreeableness.

title: Psychometric Properties of the HEXACO Personality Inventory
claimSupported: Original psychometric development and 24-facet structure of the HEXACO-PI inventory.

title: Revised NEO Personality Inventory (NEO-PI-R) and NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI) professional manual
claimSupported: 30-facet hierarchical operationalization of the Five-Factor Model.

title: A general factor of personality: Evidence for the Big One in the five-factor model
claimSupported: Higher-order General Factor of Personality (GFP) extracting shared evaluative variance.

title: Society and the adolescent self-image
claimSupported: Unidimensional global self-esteem construct and 10-item Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES).

title: Adolesanlarda benlik saygısı
journalOrPublisher: Hacettepe Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi Psikiyatri Anabilim Dalı Uzmanlık Tezi
claimSupported: Seminal Turkish adaptation of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES) in Turkish adolescent/adult sample.

title: Self-efficacy: The exercise of control
claimSupported: Theoretical framework of perceived self-efficacy and agentic control beliefs across task domains.

title: Generalized Self-Efficacy scale
journalOrPublisher: Measures in health psychology: A user's portfolio, 35-37
claimSupported: 10-item General Self-Efficacy scale (GSE) measuring global optimistic self-belief in coping with demands.

title: Turkish Adaptation of the General Perceived Self-Efficacy Scale
claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and psychometric validation of the GSE scale (internal consistency alpha = 0.86).

title: The development and validation of a scale to measure self-compassion
claimSupported: Development and 6-factor structure of the 26-item Self-Compassion Scale (SCS).

title: Öz-Şefkat Ölçeğinin Türkçeye Uyarlanması: Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and 6-factor psychometric validation of the Self-Compassion Scale in Turkish university sample.

title: Self-concept clarity: Measurement, personality correlates, and cultural boundaries

title: Benlik Belirginliği Ölçeği Türkçe Formunun Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
claimSupported: Direct Turkish psychometric adaptation of the Self-Concept Clarity Scale (N=312, alpha = 0.89).

title: Generalized expectancies for internal versus external control of reinforcement
claimSupported: Seminal conceptualization of internal vs external locus of control expectancies.

title: Rotter'in İç-Dış Kontrol Odağı Ölçeğinin üniversite öğrencileri için güvenirliği ve geçerliği
claimSupported: Turkish psychometric adaptation and validation of Rotter's Internal-External Locus of Control Scale in Turkish sample.

title: Contingencies of self-worth
claimSupported: Conceptualization of domain-contingent self-worth (academics, appearance, approval, virtue).

title: The authentic personality: A theoretical and empirical conceptualization and the development of the Authenticity Scale
claimSupported: Tripartite authenticity model: authentic living, accepting external influence, and self-alienation (12 items).

title: Self-discrepancy: A theory relating vulnerability and affect
claimSupported: Empirical formulation of Actual-Ideal discrepancies producing dejection/sadness and Actual-Ought producing agitation/anxiety.

title: Individual differences in two emotion regulation processes: Implications for affect, relationships, and well-being
journalOrPublisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 85(2), 348-362
claimSupported: Process model of emotion regulation and 10-item Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) with two distinct subscales.

journalOrPublisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 54(6), 1063-1070

title: Affect intensity as an individual difference characteristic: A review
claimSupported: Affect Intensity Measure (AIM) assessing typical magnitude and strength of emotional responses independent of valence.

claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and 6-factor structure of the DERS inventory (N=338, internal consistency alphas 0.75-0.90).

title: The Distress Tolerance Scale: Development and validation of a self-report measure
claimSupported: 15-item Distress Tolerance Scale (DTS) assessing perceived capacity to withstand negative psychological emotional states.
limitations: Higher-order composite score with 4 sub-dimensions (Tolerance, Appraisal, Absorption, Regulation).

title: Knowing what you're feeling and knowing what to do about it: Mapping the relation between emotion differentiation and emotion regulation
claimSupported: Construct validity of emotional granularity/differentiation as capacity to label discrete emotional states.
limitations: Primarily computed from ecological momentary assessment (EMA) intraclass correlation matrices rather than standard static questionnaires.

title: The twenty-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale—I. Item selection and cross-validation of the factor structure
claimSupported: 20-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20) assessing difficulty identifying feelings, difficulty describing feelings, and externally oriented thinking.

title: Toronto Aleksitimi Ölçeği (TAÖ-20) Türkçe Uyarlamasının Geçerlik ve Güvenirliği
claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and factor validation of the TAS-20 scale in Turkish clinical and non-clinical samples.
limitations: Diagnostic clinical screening history.

title: High self-control predicts good adjustment, less pathology, better grades, and interpersonal success
claimSupported: Development of the 13-item Brief Self-Control Scale (BSCS) measuring general self-regulatory capacity.

title: Brief Self-Control Scale: A study of Turkish adaptation, validity and reliability
journalOrPublisher: Dusunen Adam: The Journal of Psychiatry and Neurological Sciences, 25(3), 228-238
claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and psychometric validation of the BSCS (N=350, alpha = 0.83).

title: The Five Factor Model and impulsivity: Using a structural model of personality to understand impulsivity
claimSupported: 4-factor UPPS multidimensional model of impulsivity grounded in FFM facets.

claimSupported: Introduction of the 5-factor UPPS-P model integrating Positive Urgency.

claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and 5-factor validation of the UPPS-P Short Form in Turkish sample.
limitations: Subscale reliability varies between 0.70 and 0.84.

title: Grit: Perseverance and passion for long-term goals
journalOrPublisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 92(6), 1087-1101
claimSupported: Grit construct and 12-item / 8-item Grit Scale measuring perseverance of effort and consistency of interests.

journalOrPublisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 113(3), 492-511
claimSupported: Meta-analytic evidence demonstrating that Grit is largely redundant with Conscientiousness (rho = .84 with industriousness/persistence).

title: Kısa Azim Ölçeği'nin Türkçe Uyarlaması: Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması

claimSupported: 20-item General Procrastination Scale (GPS) measuring irrational delay of intended actions.

claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and validation of the Tuckman Procrastination Scale in Turkish adult sample.
limitations: Educational and general task context.

journalOrPublisher: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(2), 319-333
claimSupported: 24-item BIS/BAS Scales operationalizing Gray's Reinforcement Sensitivity Theory into BIS, BAS Drive, BAS Fun Seeking, and BAS Reward Responsiveness.

claimSupported: 12-item Self-Report Habit Index (SRHI) assessing automaticity, lack of conscious awareness, and behavioral history.

claimSupported: Turkish psychometric adaptation of Schwartz Value Survey validating circumplex structure and 4 higher-order value domains in Turkey.

title: Self-theories: Their role in motivation, personality, and development
claimSupported: Implicit Theories of Intelligence (Growth vs Fixed Mindset) scale assessing beliefs about malleability of human faculties.

claimSupported: 30-item Rathus Assertiveness Schedule (RAS) measuring interpersonal self-expression and rights defense.

claimSupported: 8-item Social Connectedness Scale (SCS) measuring subjective sense of interpersonal belonging and closeness with society.

claimSupported: Direct Turkish adaptation and validation of the Social Connectedness Scale in Turkish university sample.

claimSupported: DUTCH 5-factor conflict management inventory (Yielding, Compromising, Forcing, Problem Solving, Avoiding).

claimSupported: Maximization Scale assessing tendency to seek only the absolute best option versus satisficing with good-enough outcomes.

claimSupported: Direct Turkish psychometric validation of the Intolerance of Uncertainty Scale (N=375) confirming 2-factor structure (alpha = 0.93).

claimSupported: Direct Turkish psychometric validation of the Cognitive Flexibility Inventory (CFI) confirming Alternatives and Control subscales (N=420, alpha = 0.90).

claimSupported: Direct Turkish psychometric validation of MLQ (N=410) confirming 2-factor orthogonal structure (Presence alpha = 0.77, Search alpha = 0.83).

claimSupported: Sense of Coherence (SOC) scale measuring Comprehensibility, Manageability, and Meaningfulness under chronic stress.

claimSupported: Prosocial Tendencies Measure (PTM) assessing 6 types: Altruistic, Compliant, Emotional, Public, Anonymous, and Dire prosocial behaviors.

claimSupported: 21-item clinical depression symptom severity assessment inventory.

claimSupported: Unified evidentiary framework for construct validity, fairness, and psychological test norms.
limitations: General standard rather than construct-specific measurement battery.

title: Proneness to shame, proneness to guilt, and psychopathology
claimSupported: TOSCA development separating maladaptive shame from adaptive moral guilt.
limitations: Scenario-based self-report format.

title: Test of Self-Conscious Affect-3 (TOSCA-3) Turkish Adaptation
claimSupported: Turkish adaptation of TOSCA-3 with confirmed two-factor structure (alpha > 0.76).
limitations: University student sample (N=412).

title: Preliminary psychometric properties of the Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-II
claimSupported: Psychometric properties of AAQ-2 measuring experiential avoidance and psychological inflexibility.
limitations: High overlap with general distress and neuroticism.

title: Rumination reconsidered: A psychometric analysis
claimSupported: Factor analysis of RRS isolating brooding (maladaptive) from reflection (adaptive).
limitations: Self-report scale.

title: Motivated closing of the mind: 'Seizing' and 'freezing'
claimSupported: Theoretical model of epistemic freezing and urgency.
limitations: Original 42-item scale had multifactorial complexity.

title: Duygu Düzenleme Ölçeği'nin Türkçeye Uyarlanması
claimSupported: Turkish psychometric adaptation of Gross ERQ with 2-factor validity.
limitations: Sample restricted to adolescent and college cohorts.

title: Rathus Atılganlık Envanteri Geçerlik ve Güvenirlik Çalışması
claimSupported: First Turkish adaptation and validation of Rathus Assertiveness Schedule (RAS).
limitations: Historic sample requiring modern item-functioning re-verification.

title: Kısa Öz-Kontrol Ölçeği Türkçe Uyarlaması: Güvenirlik ve Geçerlik Çalışması
claimSupported: Turkish psychometric adaptation and validation of Tangney Brief Self-Control Scale (BSCS).
limitations: Evaluated in clinical and non-clinical Turkish samples (N=312).

title: Family, Self, and Human Development Across Cultures: Theory and Applications
claimSupported: The Autonomous-Relational Self model demonstrating that agency and interpersonal relatedness are orthogonal and mutually reinforcing rather than contradictory.
limitations: Theoretical monograph with supporting cross-cultural empirical chapters.

title: Bilişsel Kapanma İhtiyacı Ölçeği'nin Türkçeye Uyarlanması
claimSupported: Turkish adaptation of Kruglanski Need for Closure scale with 5 subscales.
limitations: General adult sample (N=420).
